newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Maxus Energy CEO sees 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Maxus Energy CEO sees 1996 profit.

text.p: Dallas-based Maxus Energy Corporation will turn a profit this year after steady losses since Argentine oil giant YPF SA bought it in June 1995, Maxus' top executive said Tuesday.
"Maxus will be profitable in 1996. It is already profitable at this moment," Maxus' President and CEO Roberto Monti said.

At a lunch with oil businessmen, he added Maxus attained profitability through strict financial discipline, cost cutting, rationalizing exploration strategy and higher gas production. It also benefitted from higher natural gas prices.

"Maxus was a company with very good legs but a small head. It had people with great expertise and high technology but probably mislead. What we have done is simply impose financial discipline," he said.

However, some analysts said Monti's assertion that the firm will be profitable this year should be taken with caution, pointing out that there may be big differences between the Argentine and U.S. accounting methods.
Monti also said Latin American oil companies should look for opportunities in the next five to 10 years, taking advantage of turmoil in eastern Europe.
"Once the situation in those countries becomes clearer and oil policy solidifies, they could attract huge capital inflows, compounding the future of other areas like Latin America."
